title: A11y Stitching Playbook: Token Scaling, Chart ARIA Mapping & Keyboard Stitch Tests
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Produce a concrete, testable playbook that unifies token scaling rules (density/compact modes), ARIA mapping conventions for chart/legend/table primitives, and keyboard stitching tests that can be reused by feature teams and QA. This ticket focuses on (1) authoring the playbook, (2) producing a canonical set of code examples and a small test harness, (3) running the first VPAT evidence pass for the affected components (buttons, toggles, tables, charts, legend lists), and (4) delivering a lightweight QA checklist for releases. Deliverables:
- Playbook document with decision rules for contrast tokens across density/compact scales, token overrides for high-contrast modes, and voiceover wording guidance for dynamic chart updates.
- ARIA mapping spec for charts: canvas-backed charts, svg charts and table-backed data grids: roles, live regions, focus targets, and programmatic label mapping.
- Keyboard stitching checklist: tab order primitives, arrow-key expectations inside legends and table row actions, escape/close semantics for floating toolbars.
- VPAT evidence pack: examples, annotated screenshots, test scripts, and a mapping table linking playbook rules to VPAT criteria.
- Small test harness (plain JS) for smoke tests: voiceover sequence recorder, color-contrast snapshots, and keyboard flow assertions.

Key constraints & trade-offs considered:
- We need to balance semantic ARIA richness against DOM complexity for highly virtualized tables (virtualized rows should avoid DOM bloat; we'll prioritize programmatic labeling and accessible live updates).
- Token consolidation should not force a single token for every state; instead the playbook prescribes a primary token + accessible-alternative token rule set to allow per-component overrides without deviating from auditable rules.
- VPAT evidence must be reproducible by QE; keep examples minimal and deterministic (no network data) to avoid flaky snapshots.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook doc published in Drive with review comments addressed.
- At least 3 component PRs (chart legend, compact table row, primary button) updated to follow playbook rules and merged to main. Links to PRs included in comments.
- VPAT evidence zip uploaded to Confluence and referenced from the playbook.
- Small test harness added to design-system repo under /a11y-tests with README and 3 smoke scenarios.

Problem observed: inconsistent legend focus behavior across svg/canvas charts; compact density reduces contrast below 3:1 in a few tokens. Proposed: create shared accessible-alt tokens and ARIA mapping for legends. Related: link to internal incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/a11y/incidents/chart-legend-2026-01

2026-01-28 - Diego Martinez: Ran initial audit across latest components branch. Findings attached: drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a11y-playbook-drafts. Noting two problematic patterns: (1) virtualized table row actions rely on hover-only labels, (2) legend filters lose keyboard focus when a search is applied. Adding 'keyboard-repro' label.
